tagline: Around the foot of two worn-down peaks near Kings Mountain.
intro: Sparrow Springs Road leaves US 74 just east of I-85 and curls around the foot of Crowders Mountain, and Pinnacle Road carries on, turns into Lake Montonia Road at the Cleveland County line and comes out on NC 161 near the interstate. It is eight miles and about fifteen minutes.

Both peaks are monadnocks, standing about 800 feet above the surrounding country with cliffs 100 to 150 feet high. The Pinnacle is the remnant of a quartzite ridge formed some 400 to 500 million years ago, its softer surroundings worn away. Before settlers came, buffalo grazed the land here, and the two summits marked the line between Catawba and Cherokee hunting grounds.

moments.title: Crowders Mountain
moments.text: It clears the bar for a true mountain by only a little, and when a mining company came sampling it in the early 1970s, local people talked the state into making it a park.

moments.title: The Pinnacle
moments.text: At 1,705 feet the highest point in Gaston County, the Pinnacle looks west to the Blue Ridge and east some 30 miles to the towers of Charlotte.
